changes: New: a note on the shortlist can go on a day too. Tap the note (it reads SELECTED — TAP A DAY, as a recipe does), then tap the day. It becomes an entry on that day, the same kind + OTHER makes, with the note's own words, and leaves the shortlist. Tap its tag afterwards if you want to give it a meal. Before this, a note could only be read or taken off.

New: the small tag on an entry you added with + OTHER (AD HOC, or for example DINNER · AD HOC) is now a button. Tap it to set the meal, change it, or take it off: the box that asks which meal after you cook something opens, worded for the Planner, with the entry's meal already marked; tap another meal to change it, or tap the marked one again to take it off. CLOSE leaves it as it was. Before this, changing a meal meant removing the entry and adding it again.

New: a + OTHER button on every day of the Planner adds something that is not a recipe, such as a takeaway, a meal out or leftovers. Give it a name (names you have used before are offered), and if you like the meal. It shows under that day's dishes, tagged AD HOC, with a × to take it off. It is the same entry that + ENTRY on History makes, so it is in your food diary on that day, and an entry added on History for a coming day shows on the Planner too. It is not on the shopping list and not in the Google Calendar. A week with only a takeaway in it now counts it in the PLANNED figure in the Modernist style. Taking one off a day that has not happened needs no question; for today or earlier it asks first, as History does.

Changed: tap a dish on the Planner and its recipe now opens for the number of people you set on that day. If you planned it for SERVES 20, the card says SERVES 20 (SCALED FROM 4) and the amounts are already worked out for 20, as the shopping list and the group view always were. A day with the same dish twice at different numbers opens each at its own. RESET on the card still takes you back to the amounts as the recipe is written, and opening a recipe from Recipes still starts as written. Nothing is saved by this: the recipe itself is never changed.

New: a calendar reminder now belongs to a meal, not to the whole day. Once your calendar is connected, a day with more than one meal has a REMIND ME 20:00 button on each, so a day can remind you about the dinner and not the breakfast. Dishes you have put together with GROUP SOME TOGETHER are one meal and share one reminder, on the GROUPED bar. A dish you add to a day that is in the calendar goes in without a reminder, and a side added beside its main shares the main's. Putting dishes with different reminders into one group gives them all the reminder. AUTOMATICALLY REMIND ME FOR MAIN MEALS now reminds about the meal that has the main course in it, not the whole day. In your Google Calendar a day like that is two events, one with the reminder and one without. The new buttons show once the job on the job list (C1) is done; until then the Planner is as it was.

Changed: the GROUPED bar in the Planner is now three separate buttons: the group's name, which opens it, REMIND ME, and UNGROUP. UNGROUP is a full 44-pixel button now, and answers a tap anywhere along its height. In the Modernist style the × now stays with its dish's other buttons, so a long name can no longer leave it alone on a line beneath. In Classic, a dish with a REMIND ME of its own wraps its buttons under the name instead of squeezing the name.

Changed: in the Modernist style, once your calendar is connected, the Planner's IN CALENDAR and REMIND ME buttons now sit on the same line as ADD ANOTHER, at the right-hand end of the day, instead of on a line of their own. Each day is a little shorter, so more of the fortnight fits on the screen. On a narrower window they drop under ADD ANOTHER, still at the right. ADD ANOTHER and IN CALENDAR no longer share the edge of their tap areas, and ADD THE WEEK, which was only 14 pixels tall to tap, now has the full tap area the other buttons have. A phone's layout is unchanged.

Changed: in the Modernist style, the Planner fits more of the fortnight on the tablet screen. A dish is now on one line: its name, then its course, time, SERVES, PRE-MADE and COOKED, then the ×. A name too long for the room runs onto a second line rather than being cut off, and on a narrower window the buttons drop under the name as before. ADD ANOTHER and GROUP SOME TOGETHER, a day with nothing planned, the date, the heading and the week bands each take less height. Nothing has been taken out and every button is as easy to tap as before. A phone is unchanged.

Fixed: in the Modernist style, with the tablet held upright, the Recipes cards were narrow, the History calendar ran off the side of the screen and the buttons along the top of the Shopping list did not fit. The menu down the side now folds to its narrow strip on every screen up to 1100 pixels wide, as it already did for the Planner and for a recipe being cooked, and tapping the strip opens the full menu. The Shopping buttons wrap onto a second row if they need to, and in History the month's name is smaller held upright so that the two arrows sit either side of it on one line. A computer window narrower than 1100 pixels gets the same strip.

New: in the Planner, taking a dish off a day with its × now shows a bar in that day, “Removed…” with UNDO, for ten seconds. UNDO puts the day back as it was, with the number of people, the group it was in and the calendar and reminder switches. The bar goes if you leave the Planner or if the day is changed in the meantime. Both styles.

New: in the Modernist style, a small arrow at the top right of a recipe's table says the table goes on to the right. It stays still while you scroll the table, and goes when you reach the end. A recipe that fits has no arrow, and it is left out of EXPORT PNG and of printing.

Fixed: in the Modernist style on a tablet, the top of a recipe (its buttons and the COOK FOR bar) took about a third of the screen before the steps began. The source note, SERVE WITH and the buttons now share rows, so it takes about a quarter or less and more of the recipe shows.
Fixed: in the Modernist style, SAVE RECIPE and SAVE CHANGES in the add and edit window now stay at the bottom of the screen while you scroll, instead of sitting several screens down.
Changed: in the Modernist style, the button on a recipe card that puts it on the shortlist is now a small list-with-plus picture, like the star beside it, in place of a bare +.
Fixed: in the Modernist style, an empty day in the Planner answers a tap anywhere along its row, not only on the words CHOOSE A RECIPE.
Fixed: Settings opens each tab at its top. Before, a tab opened as far down as the one before it had been scrolled.

Fixed: some small buttons are now as easy to tap as the rest, in both styles: OUR RECIPES and the other household's recipes at the top of Recipes, MARK DAY AWAY and CANCEL when choosing a recipe for a day, and the aisle box and MERGE WITH… on each line in AUDIT on the Shopping list.

New: SHOPPING LIST, at the top of a recipe beside + SHORTLIST, shows what that one recipe needs to buy, sorted by aisle like the week's list. It uses the number of people COOK FOR is showing, or the recipe's own if you have not changed it. Tick things off as you go; those ticks are kept on this device only until you leave the page, and the week's own ticks are not touched. HIDE TICKED, CLEAR TICKS, EXPORT PNG and PRINT / A4 PDF work as they do on the week. BACK TO WEEK returns to the week's list, and OPEN RECIPE goes back to the recipe. The SHOPPING button in the sidebar always shows the week. A recipe from another household's library does not have the button yet.

Fixed: PRE-MADE, for a meal coming out of the freezer, was missing from the Planner in a household with nothing planned and nothing in the food diary yet, which is how a new household starts. The app now asks the database whether PRE-MADE is ready, rather than looking for it on days already saved, so the button is there from the first dish you plan, in both styles.

New: in the Modernist style's filter panel, a box above the keywords, Find a keyword, narrows them as you type. Any part of a word will do, in capitals or not. If nothing matches it says so, and Enter adds what you typed as a keyword filter; + ADD takes you to the box. The keywords are listed with the ones that are switched on first and then the most used, and the order holds while the panel is open, so a keyword does not jump away from your finger. On a computer the cursor starts in the box; on the tablet it does not, so the keyboard stays down until you tap the box or + ADD.

New: in the Modernist style, the filters on the Recipes screen now open from a FILTERS button beside the search. Course, source, sort and every keyword are in a panel that slides in from the right, and each tap changes the recipes behind it at once. What is switched on shows as a row of small chips under the search, each removed with one tap, with CLEAR ALL at the end. That leaves the recipe cards much more of the screen: on the tablet, three-quarters of it or more. Classic keeps its rows of filters exactly as before.

Fixed: in the Modernist style, on a tablet held sideways or a laptop, the cards on the Recipes screen were squashed into thin strips once there were more than a few recipes. They are back to full size, and the list scrolls. Held upright, and on a phone, the cards were already fine, and Classic was never affected.

New: ADD SEVERAL, under NEW RECIPE, adds a whole batch of converted recipes at once. Choose the file your conversions are in, or paste them all in. The app reads every one and lists what it found before adding anything: which are ready, which are held back and why (no source, no servings, nothing to cook), and which look like recipes you already have, which are left unticked. Untick any you don't want, press the button, then check each recipe as you do now. It only adds: it never changes a recipe you already have.

ADD SEVERAL asks about a source spelt differently from one you already have, as the form does, so a batch does not split a source in two. The recipes you add are not compared with their source pages for you: Settings, Library, LIBRARY CHECK lists the ones not yet compared.
A source written with a curly apostrophe (It’s) is now recognised as the same as the straight one (It's) when the app looks for a similar source, in the form as well.

When the converter turns spoons of a solid into grams, it now keeps the spoons in brackets after the weight: 2 tbsp of sugar becomes 30 g sugar (2 tbsp), so a small amount can still be measured with a spoon. Only a conversion from spoons gets the brackets; a weight the page already gave, a cup and a single tablespoon are written as before. The converter's instructions changed (version 2026-10-18.5), so the CONVERTER bar will ask your household to load the new file.

In the app, the spoons in brackets scale with the weight: for twice the people, 30 g (2 tbsp) reads 60 g (4 tbsp). Recipes already in your library are not changed; only a line converted from now on carries the spoons.

The recipe converter's instructions change once more today (version 2026-10-18.4), with your answers to the questions on the shorter rewrite, so the CONVERTER bar will ask your household to load the file again. Several recipes from one book or page now share their source, so it is asked once; the walkthrough of the flow is written only if you ask for one; a step the recipe doesn't time is marked as quick or as open-ended, never given a made-up time; and the time allowed for chopping and measuring is 5 minutes for up to 8 ingredients and 10 for more.
In the app, a line such as 1 tin chickpeas now scales to 2 tins rather than 2 tin, and is no longer called a container word in the name.

The recipe converter's instructions have been rewritten to be shorter, so each conversion uses less of the conversion project's allowance. The CONVERTER bar will ask your household to load the new file (version 2026-10-18.3), even if you loaded one earlier today.

What changes in a conversion: the reply after the recipe lists only what you need to check or answer, with no walkthrough; a tin with no weight on the page is written as 1 tin; a photo or PDF you attach comes back renamed to the recipe's title; and several recipes in one message are each converted on their own, with any questions together at the end. Nothing in the app changes.

When a recipe's source gives no overall time, the converter now works one out from the method steps and marks it. Such a time shows an EST. tag beside it, on the recipe card, in the recipe, in the Planner and in the Shortlist, and shows as est. 1 hr 45 in the TIME box when you edit it. Type a real time over it and the tag goes.

The converter's instructions changed, so the CONVERTER bar will ask your household to load the new file into the conversion project. Recipes already in the library are not touched: a recipe with no time still shows none.

A liquid now changes unit when you scale a recipe: under 15 ml it reads in teaspoons, under 50 ml in tablespoons and from 50 ml in ml. 3 tbsp of oil for twice the people reads 90 ml, and 100 ml of stock for a quarter reads 1 1/2 tbsp. Spoons are rounded to the nearest half and ml to the nearest 5 ml. A recipe still reads exactly as written until you scale it, and amounts in grams stay in grams.

The shopping list shows a liquid of 50 ml or more in ml, with the recipes' own amounts after it, e.g. 145 ml (100 ml + 3 tbsp). Under 50 ml it stays in spoons. Spices and pastes measured in spoons are shown in spoons as before, and no tick is lost.

The recipe converter's instructions have changed, so the CONVERTER bar will ask your household to load the new file. Liquids under 50 ml are now written in spoons (3 tbsp, 1 tsp) and from 50 ml in ml (60 ml rather than 4 tbsp). A liquid the recipe weighs, such as honey or syrup in grams, stays in grams.
Nothing in the app changes yet: recipes already in the library read as before, and the shopping list adds spoons and ml of the same liquid together, as it already did.
RESET TICKS now puts the count beside a recipe's title back to nought (MODERNIST), on a recipe and in the Group Viewer. Until now it cleared the boxes but left the old count showing.
In MODERNIST, with PREPARATION shown as steps, a step that only adds prepared ingredients is no longer drawn in black as if it joined two steps.
History's meal-base bars in MODERNIST give every meal base its own look: five colours, then the same five striped. Before, the sixth repeated the first.
The week labels on the Planner and the Shopping List in MODERNIST always say SEP for September, as the other months have three letters, whatever language the device is set to.
With a keyboard, Enter on a recipe card's star, + or tick now does what tapping it does, instead of opening the recipe. This is in both styles.

A second look for the app, MODERNIST, beside the one you know, now called CLASSIC. Choose it in Settings, on the APP tab, under STYLE. It is flat and square, set in one typeface, with red kept for the main action and for what is switched on. Everything works the same in both, in light and dark, and the choice is for this device only.

In MODERNIST the side menu folds to a narrow strip on the Planner and while cooking, the Planner's shortlist can fold away to give the days more room, and the tick on a recipe card takes a recipe off the shortlist. The how-to guide in Settings, on the HELP tab, says more.
CLASSIC looks just as it did, apart from the new STYLE choice in Settings.

Every corner in the app is now the same. The round buttons, pills and circles (the star and + on a recipe card, the servings buttons, the cooking-mode switch and its dot, the + beside each day in the Planner, the SERVES and COOKED labels and the numbered set-up steps) are now rectangles with the same slightly rounded corners as everything else.
Nothing moves or changes size: only the corners are different.

You can now see where the keyboard is: press Tab and the box, button or link that has focus gets a clear plum outline. That includes the search box, the keyword box, the Shortlist name box, the boxes on the add-a-recipe screen and the ones in Settings, which showed no sign of focus before. Tapping into a text box draws the outline too.
In the side menu the outline is drawn inside each link, so the edge of the menu no longer cuts it off.

Buttons are bigger and easier to hit with a thumb: every button on a recipe, in the Planner and in the side menu is now fingertip-sized, including the small × buttons, the filter chips, the servings buttons and the cooking-mode switch. The star and + on a recipe card look the same but answer a tap in a larger area, and the search bar can be tapped anywhere along its height.

Some screens take a little more room: the filter area and the buttons above a recipe are taller, and the Planner is longer, though its rows now sit closer together. The side menu's spacing was tightened to keep it on one screen.

Writing is bigger and easier to read everywhere: nothing is smaller than 13, and the labels and buttons that were tiny are now a comfortable size. They are set in the page's own font instead of spaced-out typewriter capitals. Quantities, times and counts keep their typewriter figures.
Ticked ingredients and steps are struck through on a plain tint instead of being faded, with a bigger tick, and a step's words now sit flush left in its box.
Some things take more room as a result: the buttons above a recipe can run onto another line, and the ingredient list is a little taller.

Small grey text is darker and easier to read, in both the light and the dark theme: the labels above the filters, the counts, the line under a recipe's title and the small words in the sidebar. In the dark theme the pale shading behind quantities, today's row in the Planner, the buttons that are switched on and the warning boxes now show, and selected text is highlighted. Nothing moves and nothing is renamed.

OFTEN WITH: a recipe now names what you have grouped it with before, any course, the most often first, two at most. On the Planner a + under the dish adds one to the day and groups it with the dish, as SERVE WITH does; × hides it until you next open the app.

On the Planner, a dish that asks to be served with something you have a Side recipe for shows SERVE WITH: and a + button for each side. One tap puts the side on that day, for as many people as the dish, and groups the two so they open together, timed to finish together. × hides the offer until you next open the app.

A recipe that says to serve it with something, such as rice or naan, now shows SERVE WITH: and the name of a Side recipe in your library that fits, under its chips. Tap the name to open it. Up to three are shown, the one you cook most first. A side needs its course set to Side and the word in its title or keywords.

Cooking several dishes together: above the group's timeline, FINISH TOGETHER lines the dishes up to be ready at the same moment. The longest dish says START FIRST and each shorter one when to begin it (START AT +45 min, say), and the last mark reads SERVE. START TOGETHER is the old view. A group with a Side opens finishing together; any other starts together. Nothing is saved.

New in Settings → APP: PREPARATION. Choose AS STEPS IN THE FLOW and a line such as "leeks, thinly sliced" gets a step of its own in the recipe's diagram, beside the step before the one that needs it, so you can chop while something cooks. It is for this device only; the recipe, the timeline and the shopping list don't change.

In Settings → INGREDIENTS each list folds under its name, which shows how many it holds. Tap the name to fold or open it, and this device remembers. Typing in the lookup box now narrows every list at once.

AUDIT at the top of the shopping list shows the tools for fixing it: MERGE WITH…, the Same as …? questions, and a new aisle picker on every row, with UNDO. Off, the list is just the list, and the button says how many questions are waiting. Each device remembers which.
Merging two rows on the list when only one is ticked now unticks the merged row, after saying so, so nothing still to buy is hidden.
PRINT / A4 PDF now leaves ticked items off the shopping list, as EXPORT PNG already did, and both leave off an aisle with nothing left to buy. The PNG no longer shows MERGE WITH… links.
A recipe's source photos and PDFs are numbered FILE 1, FILE 2 and so on, instead of PAGE: a PDF of several pages is one file, kept whole.

When the recipe converter's instructions change, a CONVERTER bar asks your household to load the new file into its conversion project in the Claude app. Tap DONE once it's done, on any device; LATER hides it until the app is next opened. It never stops you using the app.
A sentence in the method or notes that starts with "Merge", "Stage" or "Group" is no longer reported as a line the app couldn't read.
Pints, quarts, ounces, pounds, fl oz and sticks of butter are now flagged as not metric when you check a recipe, as cups already were.
Two groups with the same name, or a step named like a group still in use, now show an error in the recipe's diagram instead of being drawn wrong.
Scaling a recipe keeps units as you wrote them (1 L stays L), and leaves a pinch, dash or handful alone unless it comes to a whole number.
The shopping list shows "tinned" when that's what the recipe says; it still adds up with "canned".
The dictionary now recognises long-grain rice, sweet paprika, coriander powder and free-range eggs, and word matches made one after another now all lead to the last name.
Changing the day weeks start on asks first, and clears the shopping ticks it would otherwise leave stuck in the old weeks.
Saving a recipe no longer undoes a favourite starred on another device, and changing one setting no longer changes the others back.
A recipe picture changed while RE-HOST EXTERNAL IMAGES was running keeps the change.
A shared recipe you have already added is recognised even when its web address is written slightly differently.
Restoring a backup no longer fails on a word match or shopping aisle set on another device since.
A change saved while the connection was failing can no longer be overwritten later by an older one when both finally go through.
A meal type chosen while the diary entry itself hadn't saved yet is now kept, and arrives after it.
A diary entry removed while it was still failing to save no longer comes back.
Deleting a recipe no longer turns other PRE-MADE dishes on the same days back into fresh ones.
REMOVE on a meal from the freezer in History also takes PRE-MADE off that dish, so it doesn't come back.
Changing a PRE-MADE dish's meal (dinner to lunch) changes it in the food diary too.
FOLD INTO NOTES keeps the note until the recipe's save has gone through.
A recipe picture that can't be loaded shows PHOTO CAN'T BE SHOWN instead of a broken image, and a missing source photo says to add it again through EDIT.
A save the server refuses now says so, instead of blaming the connection.
Settings → HELP shows the app's version and what's new, and an open tab now says when a new version is out: tap RELOAD.
UPLOAD PHOTO in the edit form: a picture of your own for a recipe, instead of a web link.
A FROZEN section at the end of the shopping list: an ingredient line that says frozen goes there by itself, and FROZEN can be chosen in Settings → SHOPPING AISLES.
PARSE & PREVIEW says what it read and scrolls down to the preview.
Steps under a minute read in seconds: 20 sec, not 0.3 min.
KEEP AWAKE is now called COOKING MODE.
Drink is a course, for a cocktail or a milkshake.
Finishing the recipe of a dish marked PRE-MADE for today asks: cooked fresh, or from the freezer?
On a phone, the Planner keeps each dish's name readable.
PRE-MADE on a Planner dish: a meal from the freezer goes into the food diary by itself on its day, and comes off the shopping list.
COOKED ✓ on the Planner logs a meal cooked without ticking through its recipe.
The how-to guide explains how to convert your own recipes for the app.
A weekly backup of everything to your own Google Drive: Settings → APP → BACKUP TO GOOGLE DRIVE.
Sharing recipes between households: browse another household's recipes, cook from them, and ADD TO OUR RECIPES to keep a copy.
